note: After Emerson's (1925) original description of the new species (in English); this species is the type species of the subgenus Angularitermes (later raised to genus), the subgenus Angularitermes being established in the same work on the grounds that the soldier head shape and mandibles clearly differ from those of the subgenera known at the time and that the rostrum is enormous relative to the head capsule. Both alate and soldier are fully described and measured. Page order is displaced in the OCR: the caption of figure 75 is printed before the genus-level discussion, and the table headings and values are separated; assignments were checked against the context.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head dark brown, sparsely covered with long hairs; oval, the posterior margin behind the compound eyes angular in dorsal view, with a conspicuous swelling above the compound eyes in lateral view. Fontanelle pore oval, about as long as an ocellus. Antennae yellowish brown, segment 3 about as long as segment 2, segment 4 slightly longer than segment 3. Compound eyes large, close to the lower margin of the head. Ocelli relatively large, separated from the compound eyes by slightly less than their own width. Labrum pale yellow. Postclypeus slightly paler than the head, less than half as long as its own width, strongly arched, with a median suture. Pronotum almost as dark as the head, with a pale spot near each anterior corner and two contiguous pale spots near the middle of the posterior margin; nearly triangular, the corners rounded, the sides straight and strongly convergent posteriorly; pronotum narrower than the head. Mesonotum and metanotum paler than the pronotum, posterior margin broadly concave. Abdominal tergites about the same colour as the pronotum.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head yellowish brown, constricted behind the antennae; densely covered with setae. Antennae concolorous with the head, 14-segmented, segment 3 1.5 times as long as segment 2, segment 4 equal to or slightly longer than segment 3. Mandibles with a long point, the left mandible with an extremely minute tooth near the base, the right mandible without a tooth at the base. Rostrum darker than the head, densely covered with short hairs from the constriction of the head capsule to the apex; very large and long, thick at the base—the author called it the most extreme development of the rostrum among all the nasute soldiers known to him. Thorax brownish yellow. Pronotum with setae at the margins and additional small hairs at the anterior margin, which is slightly concave. Legs proportionally very long. Abdominal tergites brownish yellow, densely covered with long setae.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Alate measurements (mm): head length 1.50—1.60; head width 1.36—1.43; compound eye diameter 0.43; pronotum length 0.70—0.73, width 1.20—1.26; hind tibia length 2.17; queen body length 12.00, abdominal width 3.00. Soldier measurements (mm): body length 6.00—6.50; head length 2.69—2.73; head width 1.00—1.10; antennal length 3.20—3.30; pronotum width 0.63—0.73; hind tibia length 2.13—2.33. Type locality Kartabo, British Guiana; known only from the type locality; holotype a soldier, morphotype a king; described from one king and queen pair and numerous soldiers of two colonies.
